summary: Full backend + frontend testing of multi-tenant CMS. 25/26 pytest pass (96%). All public landings (uk/ua/de/fr/us) render with correct currency/authority/company-type. Lead dialog, admin login, dashboard (5 countries), country edit (all 5 tabs), B2BHub MOCKED panel, and 401-redirect all work end-to-end.

minor.issue: Brute-force lockout (5 failures -> 429) did NOT trigger when tested through the public preview URL. After 6 wrong-password attempts with the same email, the API kept returning 401 instead of 429. RCA: the rate-limit identifier is `request.client.host:email`, and behind the Kubernetes ingress `request.client.host` resolves to the per-request proxy/pod IP — which can vary between requests, so each attempt is counted against a different key and the threshold of 5 is never reached for the same client/user. The brute-force guard is effectively bypassed for real internet traffic. Fix suggestion: use `X-Forwarded-For` (left-most IP) or `X-Real-IP` when present, or key the counter only on email (with a small per-IP secondary counter).

issues: Radix Dialog console warning: Missing `Description` or `aria-describedby` on DialogContent. Cosmetic / a11y only — add a <DialogDescription> or aria-describedby.

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout to work behind a reverse proxy: respect X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP, or key the lockout primarily on the email (and not on client IP) so the 5-attempt threshold is actually reachable from real internet traffic.
Add <DialogDescription> (or aria-describedby) to LeadDialog and AddCountryDialog to clear the Radix a11y warning.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: `request.client.host` is used directly for the brute-force key. Behind an ingress/proxy this is the proxy IP, not the real client, so the rate-limit doesn't accumulate per real user. Use X-Forwarded-For or X-Real-IP header (with a trusted-proxy allow-list).
server.py uses deprecated FastAPI `@app.on_event('startup' / 'shutdown')`. Migrate to `lifespan` context manager (Starlette deprecated `on_event` in 0.91+).
PATCH /api/admin/countries/{id} accepts a raw Dict[str, Any] body — no validation. A typed Pydantic model (subset of CountryIn with all-optional fields) would prevent accidental garbage writes.

AdminCountryEdit / Field components: did not see `data-testid` on the brand-name input (selector lookup `input[name='brand_name']` returned no match). Add data-testid to all Field inputs to help test automation.

seed_countries() writes the same default content blob into landing_content even when slug already exists in countries but content is missing — currently it only seeds when country itself is missing. Edge case: if landing_content is wiped but country survives, public landing falls back to a transient default; safer to upsert content separately.

rca_of_the_issue: Brute-force lockout: server.py:263 uses `request.client.host` as part of the identifier. In production-style deploys behind a reverse proxy (Kubernetes ingress here), this returns the proxy's IP and may vary per request depending on which proxy/pod terminates the connection, so the per-(ip,email) counter never reaches 5. Verified: 6 consecutive wrong-password POSTs to /api/auth/login against the public URL each returned 401, none returned 429. Mitigation: read X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP (configure a trusted-proxy list) or use email-only as the lockout key with a per-IP secondary safeguard.
